weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Ground the answer in Genesis itself (e.g., Gen 2:16, 'of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat': one boundary in a garden of yes) instead of hypothetical analogies built on commandments given centuries later.

weakest_line: So why did Samson's strength keep working?
one_fix: Land the final answer on the single sharpest idea, that power still working is not proof of God's approval, tied to 'he did not know that the LORD had left him', instead of the generic 'it came from God, for God's purpose' plus a second idea.

weakest_line: So the next time someone asks you where Cain's wife came from, you'll know what to say.
one_fix: Replace the 'you'll know what to say' close with the obvious follow-up objection (why close-relative marriage wasn't harmful or forbidden then) and end on a real question that invites comments.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Cut the Exodus backstory and spend the time actually answering 'why blood': quote Exodus 12:13 ('when I see the blood, I will pass over you'), explain the lamb dying in the firstborn's place, and why the lintel and doorposts.
Open on the specific puzzle in the text, 'Why would an all-knowing God ask Adam where he was?', instead of a devotional question aimed at the viewer, and cut the 'you skip church' sermon lines.

weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Cut one of the stacked closing quotations (Pascal or John 20:29) so the Kierkegaard parable and golden-calf evidence carry the answer, and end directly on the comment question without the channel welcome.
Cut the colleague/job analogy and use that time on the Peter-versus-Judas contrast, which is the stronger and more original landing.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Actually answer the 'forever' half of the hook with a specific text, instead of stacking familiar invitation verses (and don't present Revelation 3:20 as 'how the Bible ends').

weakest_line: So, let's allow the Bible to answer it.
one_fix: Build the whole video on one central answer (Cornelius: God sent the gospel to a man reaching for Him with the light he had), and drop the third answer and the survey of views so it fits the format.

weakest_line: Work in that world would feel like tending something you love.
one_fix: Anchor the speculation in one surprising textual detail (e.g., the tree of life and why access to it was cut off) so it delivers something new rather than a familiar list of what sin broke.
